_what_this_is: What each storage-location code in your stock export means.
A warehouse export is one row per SKU x storage location. `01` is usually
sellable stock, `02` is usually material under quality inspection, and other
codes are blocked, consignment or transfer staging. Nothing in the export says
so — the meaning of a location code is master data you hold and the ERP report
Only `sellable` nets into the planning position. Everything else is summed into
reported columns (`qty_quarantine`, `qty_blocked`, ...) so the stock stays
_why_this_is_required: Until this file existed the pipeline summed every location into one position.
That is wrong in one direction and it is the expensive one: quarantine stock
counted as available overstates the position, so the run orders *less* than it
should and the shortage arrives later, with no sign on the report that anything
So there is no default. A snapshot carrying more than one location code with any
of them undeclared is refused, and the refusal names the codes and the quantity
sitting behind each one. A single-location snapshot needs nothing declared:
there is nothing to separate, and the snapshot is the position by construction.

_statuses.sellable: on hand and available to sell — nets into the planning position
_statuses.quarantine: under quality inspection — present, not available
_statuses.consignment: on site but not owned until consumed
_statuses.in_transit_staging: staged for a transfer, not available at this node

_the_wildcard: "*": "sellable" declares every code sellable at once. It exists because a
bin-level export can carry dozens of codes that genuinely are all sellable, and
refusing to run until forty lines are typed gets the file filled in carelessly,
which is worse. It is reported on every run that uses it, so a blanket answer
stays visible as a blanket answer rather than passing for an inventory of codes.
A code named explicitly wins over the wildcard, so `"*": "sellable"` plus
`"02": "quarantine"` is the common case: everything sellable except inspection.
